references.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

rows.label: match
rows.reason: Both identify the same bug: using === to compare two Dayjs objects compares references not values, always returning false. The reference explicitly calls out this exact line and suggests .isSame() as the fix.

rows.label: match
rows.reason: Both identify the same bug: start and end are computed identically (slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()) so the working hours check is always incorrect. The reference calls it 'incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime'.

rows.label: false_positive
rows.reason: The code at line 579 uses optional chaining (userSchedule?.timeZone) so accessing timeZone on an undefined userSchedule is already safely handled and will not cause a runtime error.

rows.label: uncertain
rows.reason: The inconsistency between dayjs(override.start.toString()) and dayjs(override.start).utc() is a real stylistic concern, but the functional impact is unclear since both parse the same Date object; the claim of 'subtle timezone parsing issues' is not concretely demonstrated by the diff.

rows.label: uncertain
rows.reason: The observation that the new test lacks edge-case coverage (midnight-spanning overrides, partial overlaps) is subjective test-quality advice rather than a concrete defect introduced by the diff.
